**The argument — TTW reference notes**

Stone treats the Brendan Sorsby saga as mostly resolved and turns to Texas Tech defending its Big 12 title. He calls quarterback the clear question but reports every indication that Will Hammond will be ready for the Sept. 5 opener against Abilene Christian after tearing an ACL the previous October. He argues Hammond is not a novice, having started the 2024 Liberty Bowl against Arkansas and two games last season relieving an injured Behren Morton, and says that with Hammond healthy Texas Tech projects as a double-digit favourite in all twelve regular-season games.

*Rests on:* quarterback (Hammond's health and experience)

**The argument — TTW reference notes**

Stone frames this as a coaching-experience edge in a single game: Utah's longtime defensive coordinator Morgan Scalley is a first-time head coach, while BYU's Kalani Sitake — who worked alongside Scalley in Salt Lake City for nearly a decade — enters his eleventh season. He also believes BYU has the better roster, citing sophomore quarterback Bear Bachmeier's surprising true-freshman year and senior back LJ Martin's 1,305 rushing yards in 2025, whom he calls one of the nation's most underappreciated. Against that he sets Utah's questions on both lines, and notes BYU is 23-4 straight up over two seasons. He likes BYU to win outright in Salt Lake City.

*Rests on:* coaching experience gap; quarterback (Bachmeier); running back (Martin); opponent's offensive and defensive lines
